I’m looking for a tool or app that can help me manage and replenish my inventory more efficiently.

Ideally, I want something that can:

  • Suggest which products I need to reorder

  • Recommend how much quantity to order based on sales trends or stock levels

  • Possibly provide low stock alerts or automated reorder points

Does anyone have any recommendations or tools they’ve used for this purpose?

Hi @WestuiMerchant ,
For smart inventory management and reordering, here are some great Shopify apps to consider:

  • Assisty – Inventory Management: AI forecasting, reorder suggestions, low-stock alerts.
  • Stockbot Inventory Forecasting: Suggests what and how much to reorder.
  • Merchbees Low Stock Alert: Sends alerts when items hit custom stock levels.
  • Sumtracker: Includes purchase orders, forecasting, and multi-channel sync.

Recommendation: Start with Assisty or Stockbot - both give smart reorder recommendations, alerts, and trend analysis without needing complex setup.

posts.cooked:
The two questions — what to reorder and how much — come from the same math:

  • What/when: reorder point = (avg daily sales × lead time) + safety stock. On-hand
    below that = reorder now.
  • How much: enough to cover your order cycle + lead time — roughly
    (avg daily sales × (lead time + days between orders)) − current stock.

The trick is basing “avg daily sales” on real recent velocity per variant, not a
flat threshold — otherwise slow and fast movers get treated the same.

Do you want it broken down per variant, or rolled up at the product level?

Hi there

It sounds like you’re looking for two slightly different capabilities:

Inventory forecasting/replenishment, which helps predict what and when to reorder, and inventory synchronization, which helps keep stock levels accurate once inventory starts moving.

For forecasting and reorder recommendations, there are several inventory planning tools that analyze historical sales and suggest replenishment quantities. Many of them also offer low-stock alerts and reorder points based on sales velocity.

One thing I’ve learned is that forecasting alone isn’t enough if you sell the same inventory through multiple products, bundles, channels, or marketplaces. In those situations, keeping inventory synchronized becomes just as important as knowing what to reorder.

We’ve found that using a forecasting tool alongside an inventory sync solution works well. For example, tools like Easify Inventory Sync help ensure stock levels stay accurate across related products and bundles, reducing the risk of overselling while you’re managing replenishment.

I’m curious what type of store you run—single-channel Shopify, multiple marketplaces, bundles, or multi-location inventory? That would help narrow down which inventory planning tools might be the best fit.

One thing I’d look for in a replenishment tool is whether it considers both sales velocity and current stock at the variant level, rather than just flagging products that are low in stock. With stores carrying lots of sizes, colours, or other variants, it makes a big difference to know exactly which variants to reorder and in what quantities.

We’ve been working on this problem with specialty running stores, where getting the right sizes in stock is particularly important. The best solution will depend a bit on the type of products you sell.

What type of products are you selling?

For anyone still comparing: most of these tools use the same basic math. Reorder when stock covers less than daily sales x (supplier delivery days + safety days). Two details make a big difference in practice:

  • Leave out the days a product was sold out when you calculate daily sales. Otherwise sold-out products look slow and get under-ordered again.
  • Add supplier holidays to the delivery time. Chinese New Year alone can close factories for weeks.

Disclosure: I built Restock, which does this per variant every morning, with a “Why?” button that shows the math behind each quantity, and a free check of which stock-outs cost you sales in the last 12 months.
